title: SDLC authorization evidence capture procedure
author: Mei Chen
content:
Overview
--------
This procedure defines the minimum evidence capture and retention requirements that must be executed as part of Redwood's secure SDLC for any change that affects authorization (RBAC/attribute-based rules), authentication flows, or audit logging. It unifies pre-release gates, release-time capture, and incident-time forensics into a single, actionable playbook so that compliance evidence is consistent and audit-ready.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all code and infra changes that modify: policy definitions (role/policy docs), authorization services (redwood-authz), token issuance/authn services, audit log producers (edge-audit, ingest-audit-pipeline), and deployment of model-serving endpoints that include tenant isolation logic.
- Excludes purely UI cosmetic changes with zero auth/permission impact (owner: engineering lead must attest).

Definitions
-----------
- Evidence bundle: Atomic collection of artifacts (logs, policy snapshots, config manifests, signatures) representing a release or incident timeline.
- Capture point: A defined lifecycle moment where artifacts must be captured (pre-merge, CI gate, pre-release, post-deploy, incident start).
- Evidence Orchestrator: Service that assembles and signs evidence bundles for audit requests (internal service: evidence-orchestrator).

Roles & Ownership
-----------------
- Change owner (engineer): Executes pre-merge steps and attaches evidence links to the PR.
- Release manager (platform): Validates release-gate checklist and triggers retention tagging.
- Security oncall (security): Reviews evidence for high-risk changes and coordinates capture during incidents.
- Compliance lead (legal/security): Requests full evidence bundles during audits.
- SRE (runtime): Ensures audit-log producers are healthy and that the ingest-audit-pipeline backfills gaps.

SLOs and acceptance criteria
----------------------------
- Evidence completeness: 95% of releases with auth-impact must include a complete evidence bundle at merge (tracked by CI metric).
- Capture latency: Post-deploy evidence bundle assembled within 10 minutes of successful rollout for standard releases; within 2 minutes for high-risk (P0) changes.
- Audit log availability: No more than 5 minutes of producer downtime without backfill; backlog must be reconciled within 24 hours.

Evidence categories and retention (summary table)
------------------------------------------------
| Artifact Type | Producer / Location | Minimum retention | Notes |
|---------------|---------------------|-------------------|-------|
| Policy snapshot (RBAC/ABAC) | git://redwood/policies (tags) | 7 years | Signed tag and commit hash required |
| Access decision logs | edge-audit -> ingest-audit-pipeline | 2 years (tenant public) / 7 years (enterprise regulated) | Indexed by request_id, user_id, role_id |
| Token issuance records | authn-service logs / KMS audit | 1 year | Include ephemeral credential metadata |
| CI build manifests | CI artifact store (ci-artifacts) | 3 years | Must include diff against previous release |
| Deployment manifests | deploy-registry | 3 years | Include promoted image digest and rollout policy |
| Evidence bundle (signed) | evidence-orchestrator/archives | 7 years | PKI-signed, immutable storage |

Note on data residency: retention durations above may be shorter where legal/regulatory constraints apply (see Data Residency Mapping section). Evidence bundles for customers with residency requirements must be stored in the customer's region-specific archive endpoint.

Pre-merge checklist (required for PRs that touch auth)
-----------------------------------------------------
1. Ensure policy change is committed to git in a dedicated policy file and include a one-line summary in PR title.
2. Run local policy lint: `tools/policy-lint --path policies/` (CI gate will also run).
3. Attach a policy-impact statement in PR description (owner: author), including: affected roles, expected decision changes, and roll-back plan.
4. Add test vectors: minimal positive/negative authorization tests (unit or integration) stored in `tests/authz/` with deterministic seeds.
5. Confirm that access-decision logging is enabled in the change (feature flag `authz.log.decisions`).
6. Tag PR as `authz-impact` to trigger security-oncall review when required.

Release gate procedure (numbered)
--------------------------------
1. CI runs full authz integration suite and produces: policy snapshot, test run artifacts, and access-decision regression diff.
2. Release manager validates evidence artifacts are present and attaches evidence bundle reference (e.g., `evidence://bundle/20260115/abcd1234`).
3. Evidence Orchestrator collects: policy git commit, CI artifacts, deploy manifest, and signs the bundle.
4. Bundle index entry is written to `evidence-index` (searchable via internal UI).
5. Platform triggers `ingest-audit-pipeline` to confirm live producers are emitting access decision logs for the release.

Incident evidence collection runbook (for auth incidents)
------------------------------------------------------
Immediate actions (first 15 minutes):
1. Security oncall declares incident and records incident ID in the incident channel (e.g., INC-2026-042).
2. Freeze related changes (blocking deploys to impacted services).
3. Execute evidence collection command: `evidence-cli collect --incident INC-2026-042 --services redwood-authz,authn-service,edge-audit`
4. CLI will snapshot: current policy commits, active feature flags, recent deployment manifests (past 24h), and a configurable window of access-decision logs (default = last 6h).
5. Evidence Orchestrator streams the bundle to the incident archive and notifies security oncall when signature completes.

Deep forensic steps (post-incident):
- Reconstitute timeline by ordering: deployment digests, policy changes, request traces (correlate by request_id), and external telemetry (IDS/WAF).
- If required by the legal team, export a redacted bundle for third-party review; redaction rules are defined in Appendix B.

Exception handling and risk acceptance
-------------------------------------
- If a required artifact is missing (e.g., producer downtime prevents log capture), the change owner must file an Access Evidence Exception (AEE) in the risk register and attach a compensating control:
  - Example compensating controls: extended live traffic tracing for 72 hours, additional manual attestation from service owner, or retaining request-level tracebacks in a privileged cold store.
- AEEs are approved by the security manager and logged in the `risk-exceptions` register with a TTL (max 90 days) and required evidence to be collected.

Audit log schema (recommended minimal fields)
---------------------------------------------
We publish a compact JSON event for access-decision logs. Fields are typed and MUST be present for any auth-related decision. Example schema (formatted):

{
  "timestamp": "2026-01-15T15:12:03Z",
  "event_type": "access_decision",
  "request_id": "req-1234abcd",
  "service": "redwood-authz",
  "resource": "models:deploy:tenant-42:invoke",
  "principal": {"type": "service_account", "id": "svc-model-proxy-7"},
  "decision": "DENY",
  "policy_version": "commit:abcd1234",
  "attributes": {"ip": "198.51.100.12", "region": "us-west-2", "tenant_id": "tenant-42"},
  "trace_id": "trace-9876",
  "ingest_offset": "kafka-0-15432",
  "signature": "base64sig=="
}

Important: logs must not contain PII. If an event would include user content, the producer must redact or hash at source and include a reference pointer to the redaction key stored in the evidence bundle.

Data residency and retention mapping (short guide)
------------------------------------------------
- For global customers flagged with `geo-residency: EU`, evidence bundles and indexed logs must be replicated to the `eu-archive` storage region.
- The Evidence Orchestrator accepts a `--residency` flag at bundle creation time. Examples: `evidence-cli assemble --release 2026.01.15 --residency eu`
- When legal requires cross-border restrictions, only metadata (index entry) is global; full artifacts remain in-region. The retention table above is bounded by the intersection of legal requirement and product policy.

Operational automation (CI / infra integration)
----------------------------------------------
- CI plugin `ci-evidence` automatically:
  - Detects `authz-impact` tag,
  - Uploads artifacts to `ci-artifacts`,
  - Calls Evidence Orchestrator to create a draft bundle, and
  - Posts bundle reference to PR comment.
- `ingest-audit-pipeline` runs consumer health checks every 60s; failures create PagerDuty alerts to SRE with `PD: audit_consumer_down`.

Retention and legal hold process
-------------------------------
- Legal hold requests are issued by Legal with an `LH-` prefix. Evidence Orchestrator supports attaching holds: `evidence-cli hold --bundle-id bundle/20260115/abcd1234 --hold-id LH-2026-55`.
- Bundles under legal hold are moved to immutable storage and cannot be deleted until the hold is released.

Appendix A: CLI snippets and examples
------------------------------------
- Create a release evidence bundle:
  `evidence-cli assemble --release 20260115 --services redwood-authz,ingest-audit-pipeline --sign-key /keys/prod-signing`
- Collect incident snapshot (last 12 hours):
  `evidence-cli collect --incident INC-2026-042 --window 12h --out /tmp/evidence/INC-2026-042`

Appendix B: Redaction policy (summary)
-------------------------------------
- PII and customer-sensitive text must be redacted before leaving the tenant region. Redaction methods supported:
  - deterministic hash (sha256) with stored salt reference,
  - field-level removal with proof-of-omission metadata stored in the bundle.
- Redaction steps must be recorded in the bundle metadata: who performed redaction, method, and timestamp.

References and related reading
----------------------------
- See `authorization-logging-and-deprovisioning-guidance-2026` for logging edge-cases.
- See `evidence-orchestration-playbook-for-multi-region-compliance-2025` for multi-region evidence logistics.
